name: Haie Vive
tagline: The expatriate quarter near the airport
description: A residential district close to the airport with embassies, international schools, restaurants and the housing most of Cotonou's foreign community uses. It is quieter and better serviced than the rest of the city and priced accordingly.
bestFor: Anyone wanting security, services and French-speaking company
pros: Best housing and infrastructure in the city
cons: A vehicle or zemidjan is needed

name: Cadjehoun
tagline: The airport district, residential and central
description: The district around Cotonou's airport, mixing residential streets with offices and services, well positioned for both the centre and the road west towards Ouidah. It is one of the more comfortable parts of the city without Haie Vive's premium.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a middle position on price and comfort
pros: Cheaper than Haie Vive next door
Convenient for both the airport and the centre
cons: Little walkable beyond the immediate blocks

name: Ganhi and the Central Market
description: The central commercial district around the Dantokpa market, one of the largest open-air markets in West Africa, sprawling along the lagoon with everything from cloth to fetish materials. It is dense, chaotic and where the city's trade happens.
bestFor: Budget stays and anyone who wants the market on the doorstep
pros: Dantokpa, one of West Africa's great markets
cons: Real risk of theft in the crowds

name: Fidjrosse and the Beach Road
tagline: The coast west, where the bars are
description: The strip along the Atlantic west of the centre, with beach bars, restaurants and a growing residential area behind them. The sea here is beautiful and genuinely dangerous to swim in, which is the constant local warning.
bestFor: Anyone wanting the beach bars and sea air
pros: Beach bars and restaurants along the coast
Cooler and airier than the interior of the city
cons: Swimming here is dangerous and people drown

name: Ouidah
tagline: An hour west, where the history is
description: A town forty kilometres west, the historic centre of the Atlantic slave trade in this region and of Vodun practice, with the Route des Esclaves running four kilometres to the Door of No Return on the beach, the Python Temple and the Sacred Forest.
bestFor: Anyone whose reason for being in Benin is the history
pros: The Route des Esclaves and the Door of No Return
The Python Temple and the Sacred Forest
The Vodun festival on the tenth of January
cons: Fills completely for the January festival
